_comment: Differentiates the Days and times lessons, which were one lesson with the language swapped: an identical objective, a shared explanation and a verbatim-shared prompt, all in one exercise shape. Each language now teaches what its own week actually does — German names its days after the sun, the moon and old gods; Spanish keeps the Roman planets and the two church days; Portuguese counts them from domingo. Applied by scripts/content/differentiate-first-words.py.

concept.explanation: The German week is named, not numbered: Sonntag and Montag for the sun and the moon, Dienstag and Donnerstag and Freitag for old gods, and Mittwoch, the odd one out, which just marks the middle. Weekdays are masculine, so am Montag. Say morgen and you mean tomorrow; say der Morgen and you mean the morning.

lesson.objective: Meet the sun, the moon and the old gods hiding in the German week, and the one weekday that names nobody.
lesson.explanation: Most German weekdays are a small pantheon. Sonntag and Montag carry the sun and the moon; Dienstag, Donnerstag and Freitag keep the names of old gods, and only Mittwoch names nobody at all — it simply marks the middle of the week. The days are masculine, so ‘on Monday’ is am Montag. And mind the capital letter: morgen is tomorrow, but der Morgen is the morning.

exercises.prompt: A Berlin calendar marks each day with one word. Which is the word for today?
exercises.explanation: Heute is the one. Morgen, Mittwoch and Woche name tomorrow, Wednesday and the week.

exercises.prompt: Most German weekdays carry a sun, a moon or a god. Which one names nobody and simply marks the middle of the week?
exercises.explanation: Mittwoch is literally mid-week. Donnerstag thunders with Donar and Sonntag belongs to the sun.

exercises.prompt: Read the week. Which day does the passage place in the middle?
exercises.passage: Sonntag ist der Tag der Sonne. Am Montag arbeite ich. Am Dienstag lerne ich Deutsch. Mittwoch ist die Mitte der Woche. Am Donnerstag regnet es.
exercises.translation: Sunday is the day of the sun. On Monday I work. On Tuesday I learn German. Wednesday is the middle of the week. On Thursday it rains.
exercises.explanation: The fourth sentence says it outright: Mittwoch ist die Mitte der Woche.

exercises.prompt: Build the German sentence for on Monday I work, with the day in first position.
exercises.explanation: German likes the day in front: Am Montag, then the verb arbeite, then ich.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the noun for the morning, not the word for tomorrow: Der ___ ist kalt.
exercises.explanation: Der Morgen, with the capital letter and the article, is the morning; morgen alone means tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: today is Sunday.
exercises.explanation: Heute ist plus the day. Sonntag is the sun's day, the name sitting in plain sight.

exercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: Am Montag arbeite ich.
exercises.explanation: German opens with the day and puts the verb straight after it: am Montag, then arbeite.

concept.explanation: Five Spanish weekdays are the old sky names — lunes (moon), martes (Mars), miércoles (Mercury), jueves (Jupiter), viernes (Venus) — while sábado and domingo come from the Sabbath and the Lord’s day. They are masculine and lower-case, and the article el carries the meaning of ‘on’: el lunes. Mañana is tomorrow; la mañana is the morning.

lesson.objective: Five Spanish weekdays are the old planets and gods; learn which two days break that pattern.
lesson.explanation: Spanish weekdays are the Roman sky turned into a calendar: lunes is the moon, martes Mars, miércoles Mercury, jueves Jupiter and viernes Venus. Then the naming breaks — sábado comes from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord’s day. The days are masculine and lower-case, and Spanish needs no separate word for ‘on’: the article el carries it, as in el lunes. Watch out, too: mañana is tomorrow, while la mañana is the morning.

exercises.prompt: Your Madrid phone writes a label above the date. Tap the label for today.
exercises.explanation: That is hoy. The decoys mean tomorrow, Monday and the week.

exercises.prompt: Build the Spanish sentence for on Monday I work; the article carries the on.
exercises.explanation: El sits in front of the day and means on: el lunes, on Monday.

exercises.prompt: Complete the Spanish for on Mondays, meaning every Monday: ___ lunes trabajo.
exercises.explanation: Spanish uses the plural article for a repeated day: los lunes, on Mondays.

exercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it: today is Friday.
exercises.explanation: Hoy es plus the day. Viernes still carries the name of Venus.

exercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: El lunes trabajo.
exercises.explanation: There is no separate word for on here; the article el does that work in front of the day.

exercises.prompt: Five Spanish weekdays carry the name of a planet or a god. Which pair leaves that company?
exercises.explanation: Sábado comes from the Sabbath and domingo from the Lord's day; lunes to viernes are the old sky names.

exercises.prompt: Read the week. Which day does the passage name after the moon?
exercises.passage: El lunes es el día de la Luna. El martes trabajo. El miércoles estudio. El jueves llamo a mi madre. El viernes descanso.
exercises.translation: Monday is the day of the moon. On Tuesday I work. On Wednesday I study. On Thursday I call my mother. On Friday I rest.
exercises.explanation: The first line says it: el lunes is the day of la Luna, the moon.

concept.explanation: Portuguese numbers its week instead of naming it: domingo is the first feria, so Monday is segunda-feira, the second fair, running through terça, quarta, quinta and sexta-feira. The days are feminine and take na: na segunda-feira. Sábado and domingo are the exceptions, and amanhã (tomorrow) differs from manhã (morning) by one letter.

lesson.objective: Count the Portuguese week from domingo and keep the hyphens that hold segunda-feira together.
lesson.explanation: Portuguese does not name its weekdays — it counts them. Domingo, the Lord’s day, is the first of the ferias, and every working day takes its number from there: segunda-feira, the second fair, through terça, quarta, quinta and sexta-feira. They are feminine, so ‘on Monday’ is na segunda-feira, hyphen and all. Sábado keeps the Sabbath’s name instead. And note the pair amanhã (tomorrow) and manhã (morning): a single letter separates them.

exercises.prompt: In Lisbon a shop sign swaps a single word at dawn. Choose today's word.
exercises.explanation: Hoje is right. What is left over means the week, Monday and tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Predict the sentence before you write it. Monday is the second fair, so count from domingo: today is Monday.
exercises.explanation: Hoje é plus the day. Domingo is the first feria, so Monday, the second, is segunda-feira.

exercises.prompt: Give the English meaning: Na segunda-feira trabalho.
exercises.explanation: Na marks on before a feminine weekday, and segunda-feira is the second fair.

exercises.prompt: Portuguese counts the working days from domingo. Counting that way, which day is the fourth?
exercises.explanation: Domingo is the first feria; segunda is second, terça third, so the fourth is quarta-feira.

exercises.prompt: Read the week. According to the passage, which day opens the week?
exercises.passage: Domingo é o primeiro dia da semana. Na segunda-feira trabalho. Na terça-feira estudo português. Na quarta-feira descanso. Amanhã é quinta-feira.
exercises.translation: Sunday is the first day of the week. On Monday I work. On Tuesday I study Portuguese. On Wednesday I rest. Tomorrow is Thursday.
exercises.explanation: The opening line names it: domingo é o primeiro dia da semana.

exercises.prompt: Build the Portuguese sentence for today is Wednesday, keeping the hyphen.
exercises.explanation: Hoje first, then é, then the hyphenated day: quarta-feira.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the noun for the morning, not the word for tomorrow: A ___ está fria.
exercises.explanation: Manhã is the morning; amanhã, with an a in front, is tomorrow.
